ru: Мы встре́тимся в том же кафе́ ско́ро.
en_alt: We will meet at the same café soon.
note: Equally valid preposition choice for the word bank.

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло вре́мя, мы бы встре́тились ча́ще.

en_alt: She celebrated the New Year at home.
She saw the New Year in at home.
note: The idiom "see in the New Year" is right; the alts give the plainer readings.

ru: Без расписа́ния я бы встреча́ла по́езд науга́д.
note: Imperfective "would meet" is the correct half of this collision; the perfective встретить partner sits outside this packet.

ru: В аэропорту́ я бу́ду встреча́ть роди́телей.

note: Imperfective imperative; the perfective partner has a different object ("guests"), so the drill still has a cue.
Present-tense statement against a perfective imperative partner — the sentences differ well beyond the verb frame.

ru: В шко́ле они́ встреча́лись ка́ждый день.
en_alt: At school they met every day.
They meet at weekends.
They meet up on weekends.
We meet at the same café.

ru: По́сле кани́кул мы бу́дем встреча́ться ча́ще.
en_alt: After the holidays we will meet more often.

ru: Е́сли бы меня́ позва́ли, я бы вступи́ла в клуб.
Он вступи́л в клуб люби́телей книг.
За́втра он всту́пит в но́вую до́лжность.
en_alt: Tomorrow he will take up the new position.

note: Three of this word's sentences render вступить as "join"; the headword gloss "to enter" may be the half that needs widening.

en_alt: She joined the conversation.
Will you join the conversation?

ru: Без сту́ка я бы не входи́ла в чужо́й кабине́т.
Я вхожу́ в класс ро́вно в де́вять.
en_alt: I enter the classroom at exactly nine.

ru: С за́втрашнего дня го́сти бу́дут входи́ть че́рез гла́вный вход.
en: From tomorrow guests will be entering through the main entrance.
note: Imperfective будут входить rendered as a bare "will enter" collides with three perfective войти futures; the corpus renders будущее сложное as "will be V-ing" elsewhere.

en_alt: He always comes in without knocking.

ru: На встре́че мы бу́дем выбира́ть ме́сто для пра́здника.
en: At the meeting we will be choosing a place for the celebration.
en_alt: At the meeting we will be choosing a venue for the celebration.
note: Imperfective будем выбирать rendered "will choose" collides with three perfective выбрать futures; место is also plainly "place".
Imperfective imperative against a perfective one; the objects differ ("the present" vs "what you like"), so the cue survives.

en_alt: She took a long time choosing a dress.

ru: Без сове́та я бы выбира́ла до́лго.
en: Without advice I would take a long time choosing.
note: "I would choose for a long time" is not idiomatic English; this matches the sibling sentence's phrasing and keeps the imperfective.

ru: Е́сли бы вы́бор был мой, я бы вы́брал си́нее.

note: Perfective imperative; English cannot mark the aspect here and the object differs from the imperfective partner.

ru: За́втра он вы́берет себе́ но́вый телефо́н.
en_alt: Tomorrow he will choose a new phone for himself.

note: The "will choose" collision is cleared on the imperfective side (будем выбирать → "will be choosing"); this perfective future is correct.
The "will choose" collision is cleared on the imperfective side; this perfective future is correct.

ru: Мы вы́брались из ле́са к ве́черу.
Я вы́берусь в го́сти в суббо́ту.
en_alt: I will get out to visit on Saturday.
note: Matches the sibling "I will get out to the theatre".

ru: Е́сли бу́дет вре́мя, я вы́берусь в теа́тр.
Без верёвки мы бы не вы́брались из я́мы.
Е́сли бы вещь слома́лась, я бы её вы́бросил.

en_alt: I will remove the stain from the shirt.
He took the dog out into the street.
note: The English dropped на улицу altogether.

ru: Е́сли начнётся пожа́р, я вы́веду всех нару́жу.
Без проводника́ он бы не вы́вел нас из ле́са.

en_alt: His face betrayed his agitation.

ru: Без волне́ния он бы не выдава́л свои́ чу́вства.
note: Imperfective "would not give away" is the correct half of the "would give" collision; the perfective выдать sentence is the one corrected.

en: The library gives out books for free.
en_alt: The library lends books for free.
The library issues books for free.
note: "lends" is a free rendering of выдаёт and pulls the sentence away from the headword gloss "to give out".

ru: С понеде́льника банк бу́дет выдава́ть креди́ты.

en_alt: The cashier gives out money.
Do you give out money?

ru: Е́сли бы я знал секре́т, я бы его́ не вы́дал.
en: If I had known the secret, I would not have given it away.
note: Perfective бы+past is a past counterfactual — a single completed event; this also clears the "would give" collision with the imperfective выдавать sentence.

en_alt: Tomorrow the cashier will give out the wages.
The bank issued him a loan.

ru: Я вы́дам тебе́ зарпла́ту в пя́тницу.
Е́сли бы бы́ли сре́дства, мы бы вы́делили де́ньги.

en_alt: Will you allocate time?

ru: Е́сли бы пришло́сь, я бы вы́держал и бо́льше.

en_alt: Soon he will pass the last exam.
Will you pass the difficult exam?
note: The sibling sentence renders выдержал экзамен as "passed".

ru: Е́сли бы доро́га была́ свобо́дна, мы бы вы́ехали ра́ньше.
en: If the road had been clear, we would have set off earlier.
note: The two halves disagreed — a present "if the road were clear" against a past "would have set off"; the perfective reads as a past counterfactual.

en_alt: We left the city early.

ru: Е́сли бы ему́ ста́ло пло́хо, я бы вы́звал врача́.
en: If he had felt unwell, I would have called a doctor.
en_alt: If he had been taken ill, I would have called a doctor.
note: Perfective бы+past as a past counterfactual; this clears the "would call" collision with the imperfective вызывать sentence.

ru: Я вы́зову ма́стера для ремо́нта за́втра.
en: I will call a repairman for the repairs tomorrow.
note: для ремонта was dropped from the English.

ru: С за́втрашнего дня дире́ктор бу́дет вызыва́ть сотру́дников по о́череди.
en_alt: From tomorrow the director will be calling in the employees one by one.
The director calls in the employee.
This music causes sadness.

ru: Без причи́ны я бы не вызыва́ла такси́.
note: Imperfective "would not call" is correct; the perfective вызвать sentence is the side corrected.

ru: Е́сли бы повезло́, мы бы вы́играли матч.
en: If we had been lucky, we would have won the match.
note: Perfective повезло/выиграли read as a past counterfactual about a finished match; "If we were lucky, we would win" is the imperfective-flavoured reading.

ru: Они́ вы́шли из теа́тра по́сле спекта́кля.
en_alt: They came out of the theatre after the performance.

ru: За́втра она́ вы́йдет на рабо́ту по́сле о́тпуска.
Я вы́йду на у́лицу че́рез мину́ту.
Она́ вы́шла из до́ма ра́но у́тром.
en_alt: She left the house early in the morning.

ru: Ты вы́йдешь из до́ма ра́но у́тром?
en: Will you go out of the house early in the morning?
note: из дома was dropped; the sibling statement keeps it.

ru: Е́сли бы переста́л дождь, я бы вы́шел погуля́ть.
en: If the rain had stopped, I would have gone out for a walk.
note: Perfective бы+past as a past counterfactual; this clears the "would go" collision with the imperfective выходить sentence.

ru: Я вы́ключил компью́тер и лёг спать.

en_alt: Turn off the light, please.

ru: Е́сли бы я упа́л в я́му, я бы вы́лез сам.

en_alt: I will climb out of the car myself.
Will you get out of the water?

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло тяжело́, я бы не вы́несла тако́й бо́ли.
en_alt: If it were hard, I could not bear such pain.

ru: Я вы́несу ме́бель во двор за́втра.
Е́сли бы пона́добилось, я бы вы́нула но́жницы.
Че́рез мину́ту я вы́ну пиро́г из ду́ховки.
Е́сли бы я хоте́л пить, я бы вы́пил воды́.

en_alt: They drank to their friends' health.

note: Perfective imperative; the пить partners ("Drink more water", "I drink water") differ elsewhere in the sentence.

en_alt: He drank a glass of milk.
note: "drank up" is stilted on its own; the alt is what an English speaker would write.
"a glass of milk" against the partner's bare "tea" leaves the drill a cue.
